title: Go: Benchmarking
description: Write and run benchmarks in Go to measure and compare function performance.

steps.title: Basic Benchmark function
steps.description: Write a function `Sum(n int) int` that returns the sum 1..n. Create a benchmark `BenchmarkSum` that calls `Sum(1000)` in a loop `for i := 0; i < b.N; i++`. Print the benchmark result.
hints: The `b.N` value is adjusted by the framework for stable timing

verification.successMessage: Benchmark function runs and reports timing!
verification.failureMessage: Loop b.N times inside the benchmark function.

steps.title: b.N loop pattern
steps.description: Write a function `Concat(n int) string` that concatenates "a" repeated n times. Benchmark it with n=100. Print the number of iterations (`b.N`) and the result to show the pattern works.
hints: Put the setup code OUTSIDE the b.N loop — only the code to measure goes inside
b.N is determined by the benchmark framework
Reset timer if setup is expensive: `b.ResetTimer()`

verification.failureMessage: Make sure only the code to benchmark is inside the b.N loop.

steps.title: Reset timer
steps.description: Benchmark a `SortSlice(s []int)` function. Before the benchmark loop, create a large slice (10000 elements). Use `b.ResetTimer()` to exclude setup time. Print the benchmark results.
hints: `b.ResetTimer()` resets the benchmark timer to zero
Use ResetTimer after expensive setup but before the measurement loop

verification.successMessage: Timer reset excluded setup from benchmark timing!
verification.failureMessage: Call b.ResetTimer() after setup but before the loop.

steps.title: Benchmark different inputs
steps.description: Write a `Fibonacci(n int) int` (recursive). Create benchmarks `BenchmarkFibonacci10` and `BenchmarkFibonacci20` using different input values. Print the comparison.
hints: Run separate benchmarks for each input size
b.N is automatically smaller for slower functions
Compare results: Fibonacci(20) should show more ns/op than Fibonacci(10)

verification.successMessage: Benchmarks with different inputs show scaling!
verification.failureMessage: Create two benchmark functions for different inputs.

steps.title: Bench comparison
steps.description: Benchmark two implementations of `Reverse(s string) string`: one using concatenation and one using `strings.Builder`. Print both results so you can compare which is faster.
hints: Implement both versions as separate functions
strings.Builder is generally faster for string concatenation

verification.successMessage: Bench comparison shows which implementation is faster!
verification.failureMessage: Create two separate benchmark functions for each implementation.
